description: A reliable browser-based multiplayer pétanque game using standard pétanque rules, with shareable rooms and rejoinable games that do not require email invitations.

services.name: Game frontend
services.description: Responsive browser game UI for creating and joining rooms, viewing the piste and balls, taking turns, tracking scores, and rejoining through a room link.

services.name: Realtime game backend
services.description: Authoritative room and match logic, standard pétanque rules and scoring, realtime synchronization, reconnect handling, and persisted game state.

questions.question: Which language should the game frontend use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Recommended for a maintainable browser game with strongly typed game and network state.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Use standard JavaScript without static type checking.

questions.rationale: A typed frontend helps prevent client/server state mismatches in a realtime multiplayer game.

questions.question: Which framework should the game frontend use?

options.label: React
options.description: Recommended for a component-based browser game interface.

options.label: Vue
options.description: A component-based alternative with a lightweight authoring model.

options.label: Svelte
options.description: A compiler-based framework for a compact browser interface.

options.label: Angular
options.description: A full-featured framework with an opinionated application structure.

questions.rationale: React is a practical default for an interactive game board and reusable game controls.

questions.question: What frontend capabilities should the game include?
questions.recommendedChoice: A responsive game board and lobby; live turn-by-turn play for singles-only classic 1-v-1 pétanque, with three boules per player and a first-to-13-points win condition; create or join a private room with a reusable shareable link; clear turn and score guidance; reconnect and rejoin the same match without email; accessible controls and connection status.
questions.answer: A responsive game board and lobby; live turn-by-turn play for singles-only classic 1-v-1 pétanque, with three boules per player and a first-to-13-points win condition; create or join a private room with a reusable shareable link; clear turn and score guidance; reconnect and rejoin the same match without email; accessible controls and connection status.
questions.rationale: Confirmed: live turn-by-turn multiplayer, private reusable room links, singles-only classic 1-v-1, three boules per player, and first to 13 points.

questions.question: Which language should the realtime game backend use?

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: A strong fit for an Azure-hosted multiplayer backend and realtime game services.

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Use one language across the browser client and backend.

options.label: Java
options.description: Use Java for the backend service.

options.label: Python
options.description: Use Python for the backend service.

questions.rationale: C#/.NET has mature Azure support for realtime connections and durable application services.

questions.question: Which framework should the backend use?
questions.rationale: A serverless backend can handle room actions and game events while Azure SignalR Service provides realtime player updates.

questions.question: What backend capabilities should the game include?
questions.recommendedChoice: Authoritative live turn-by-turn singles-only classic 1-v-1 pétanque rules and scoring, with three boules per player and a first-to-13-points win condition; realtime room synchronization; private rooms with stable IDs and reusable shareable rejoin links; persisted match state and player seats across refreshes or temporary disconnects; safe handling of duplicate or late game actions; room cleanup and reconnect support.
questions.answer: Authoritative live turn-by-turn singles-only classic 1-v-1 pétanque rules and scoring, with three boules per player and a first-to-13-points win condition; realtime room synchronization; private rooms with stable IDs and reusable shareable rejoin links; persisted match state and player seats across refreshes or temporary disconnects; safe handling of duplicate or late game actions; room cleanup and reconnect support.
questions.rationale: Confirmed match format and rules are enforced by the authoritative backend; persisted room state and reconnect-safe actions support rejoining through a reusable private link.

questions.question: Which data stores are required?

options.label: Azure Cosmos DB
options.description: Persist room metadata, match state, player seats, and game history.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Required backing storage for Azure Functions and its AzureWebJobsStorage account.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only when the application does not need persistence, storage, queues, or service-associated storage.

questions.rationale: Persistent room and match state enables players to rejoin after disconnects, and Functions requires an associated storage account.

questions.question: Do players need to sign in to use the game?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require users to sign in to use application features.

options.label: No
options.description: Let friends join with a room link and optional display name, without creating an account.

questions.rationale: The user specifically wants to avoid repeated email-based invitations; shareable room links can provide low-friction joining without requiring sign-in.
